case_name: Denise Sadjian Curcio v. Commissioner (Kenneth Curcio, Intervenor)
suitability_reason: Stand-alone section 6015(f) equitable innocent-spouse relief case; outcome turns on a facts-and-circumstances weighing (economic hardship, knowledge) under Rev. Proc. 2013-34, not mechanical computation.

taxpayer.notes: Requesting spouse; former spouse (intervenor, an accountant) opposed relief. Married October 30, 1993; separated 2018; divorced February 2020. Amounts rounded to nearest dollar.

adjustments: No notice of deficiency: underpayment arose because 2013 overpayment of $9,645 credited to 2014 estimated tax was disallowed under section 6511; final determination letter dated December 19, 2018 denied 6015(f) relief
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Denial of section 6015(f) equitable relief from joint and several liability for 2014 unpaid tax
conceded: Respondent, shortly before trial, conceded petitioner is entitled to full relief under section 6015(f); intervenor continued to oppose

findings_of_fact.fact: 2014 joint return reported total tax $12,808, ACTC $3,000, estimated payment $9,645, balance due $163
findings_of_fact.snippet: For 2014 the couple reported total tax of $12,808, attributable to intervenor’s various items of income, offset by an additional child tax credit of $3,000

findings_of_fact.fact: 2013 and 2014 returns mailed December 12, 2017; 2013 overpayment disallowed under 6511, leaving unpaid 2014 balance $9,808
findings_of_fact.snippet: leaving an unpaid balance for that year of $9,808 (exclusive of interest and penalties).

findings_of_fact.fact: Form 8857 received June 1, 2018; monthly expenses $5,579; no income at that time
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner reported that she was not receiving any income at that time and that her monthly expenses totaled $5,579.

findings_of_fact.fact: Debts: $160,000 to cousin, $16,000 to divorce attorney, ~$100,000 credit card; settlement account exhausted by mid-2019
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner owes $160,000 to her cousin and $16,000 to her divorce attorney.

findings_of_fact.fact: Property settlement agreement: intervenor solely responsible for 2014 liability if petitioner prevails; otherwise shared equally
findings_of_fact.snippet: intervenor will be solely responsible for the unpaid tax liability for the year in issue if petitioner prevails in this action

findings_of_fact.fact: Court finds economic hardship and no knowledge/reason to know of nonpayment
findings_of_fact.snippet: we are persuaded that she would suffer economic hardship if obliged to pay the tax due for the year in issue.

issues.question: Is petitioner entitled to equitable relief under section 6015(f) from joint and several liability for the 2014 underpayment, over intervenor's objection?
issues.holding: Yes; full relief granted based on economic hardship and lack of knowledge or reason to know intervenor would not pay

amount_determined.description: 2014 unpaid balance (exclusive of interest and penalties)

issues.computable_reason: Equitable facts-and-circumstances weighing (economic hardship, knowledge) under Rev. Proc. 2013-34; discretionary

decision.text: Decision will be entered for petitioner.

notes: De novo standard and scope (petition filed March 2019, before section 6015(e)(7) effective date). Threshold conditions undisputed; not eligible for streamlined relief. Unsuitable for deficiency recomputation.
